messages:
Emma (acct): FYI ACME flagged a sudden p99 jump on their Dedicated pool during the billing window ~11:05 UTC, customer sees 3.2s p99 (normally ~450ms). They say it started right after we hit a quota burst.
Sam (support): Chatted with them — they repro with a small steady traffic ramp. Getting occasional 502s and long tails. Can we triage? @alex tagging SRE oncall. :warning:
metric-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-acme-az1 p99 latency > 2s for 5m (3135792510)
Alex (eng-sre): Looking. Initial read: provision queue for that pool spiked, attach latency increased. Could be cold-GPU respawn + image pull. Pulling traces now.
Priya (eng-runtime): Can you paste the request IDs? I want to check KV cache misses and kernel init times. If it's cold GPUs we'll see long init time in the runtime traces.
Sam (support): Customer provided request IDs: r_9a1b, r_9a1c, r_9a1d. Repro command they used:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n"
```
Emma (acct): They also attached a graph showing spike coincidence with end-of-hour billing activity and a backlog of scale requests.
Alex (eng-sre): Got traces for r_9a1b: attach start -> scheduler wait 22s -> node alloc -> image pull 14s -> runtime init 8s -> first token. That explains the >3s tail (sum of queue + pull + init). Looks like pool ran out of warmed GPUs and autoscaler queued many attaches.
Jordan (eng-platform): We're seeing a transient spike in provisioning requests for that dedicated shard (acme-prod-eu-west). Fairshare throttles engaged and min-pool was 0. Autoscaler rapid ramp hit the platform's attach rate limiter.
Priya (eng-runtime): Runtime logs show kernel cache miss leading to model weight load heavy IO. Also noticed image pull errors intermittently: `ErrImagePull: context deadline exceeded` then retry. That adds ~12s on some attaches.
Sam (support): Customer asks for immediate mitigation — what can we do now to reduce p99? They prefer no downtime.
Alex (eng-sre): Short term: 1) Increase min-pool for that reserved shard to 1-2 to keep warm GPUs. 2) Temporarily relax fairshare for high-tier accounts to allow faster attach. 3) Route overflow traffic to hosted fallback model variant if auth/contract allows. I can run 1 & 2 now.
Jordan (eng-platform): I'll bump min-pool for acme-prod-eu-west to 2 and raise attach parallelism cap for that shard for 15m window. Applying... done (3135792668).
metric-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: min-pool(acme-prod-eu-west)=2 by jordan (3135792669)
Alex (eng-sre): Also enabling proactive preload of model weights on new nodes (pre-pull) for that shard — rolling hook in platform. Priya, will runtime pre-pull patch help for next incidents?
Priya (eng-runtime): Yes — runtime pre-pull plus persistent model cache reduces init from ~8s to ~1.2s for warmed nodes. I'll open a small fast-rollout to enable pre-pull on dedicated shards with high SLA.
Sam (support): After the platform change, ACME reports p99 dropped to 520ms within ~90s. They still see a few 502s during ramp but much improved.
Emma (acct): Customer appreciated the quick mitigation, asked for a longer-term playbook so this doesn't reoccur next billing window.
Alex (eng-sre): Suggested long-term fixes: - Set non-zero min-pools for known billing-window customers - Add heuristic prewarm for scheduled heavy windows - Improve attach backoff jitter to avoid synchronized spikes - Increase registry pull concurrency and add regional image cache nodes
Jordan (eng-platform): I'll create a runbook entry (prewarm + min-pool + temporary fairshare bump) and a scheduled cron job to auto-prewarm for accounts with expected billing spikes.
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll PR runtime pre-pull + persistent cache option and add a metric for kernel weight load time so we can alert earlier.
Sam (support): Logged mitigation steps and follow-ups in the ticket. Reopen if ACME sees recurrence. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Alex (eng-sre): One action item for SRE: add an alert when attach queue length > 50 and min-pool == 0 for any reserved shard. I can take that.
Emma (acct): Noted. Also coordinating with the customer to share the runbook and confirm they want min-pool=2 permanently or scheduled.
Sam (support): Closing loop with customer now. If anyone wants to add notes for the runbook, ping me.
